subject.title: Feature: Postcondition checks for cron jobs (deterministic verification of agent outcomes)

question: Should OpenClaw support scheduler-owned cron post-run verification for agentTurn jobs, and should that live as a core CronJob postconditions field or as a fail-capable plugin hook with scheduler retry/escalation authority?
rationale: The remaining work adds public cron schema/state and can execute unattended shell checks after model work, so automation cannot safely choose the core-vs-plugin API or command-execution trust boundary.

options.title: Design Scheduler-Owned Verifier
options.body: Define a narrow additive verifier contract with explicit permissions, timeout/cancellation/redaction rules, durable state, retry context injection, and failure-alert integration before implementation.

options.title: Expose Fail-Capable Plugin Hook
options.body: Keep CronJob schema smaller and first add a plugin hook that can turn a completed cron run into a scheduler-owned retry or escalation decision.

options.title: Defer Native Verification
options.body: Document command cron and external monitoring as the current workaround and leave native postcondition verification unimplemented until maintainers are ready to own the security model.

recommendation.title: Design Scheduler-Owned Verifier
recommendation.body: Define a narrow additive verifier contract with explicit permissions, timeout/cancellation/redaction rules, durable state, retry context injection, and failure-alert integration before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history on the cron schema/runtime/docs surfaces and prior routing comments for this exact product/security boundary.
